title: Israel's Election Deadlock, Explained
description_summary: EXAMPLE PLAN (short, for testing the layout). Israel's 27 October election left neither bloc with the 61 seats needed to govern.

sources.title: Al Jazeera: Arab parties back Eisenkot

clips.caption: 53, 48 and 19: the numbers behind Israel's deadlock.

scenes.narration: On the twenty seventh of October, Israelis voted in a general election. When the count was almost finished, nobody had won. Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc had fifty three seats. Gadi Eisenkot's bloc had forty eight. To govern, you need sixty one.

The other nineteen seats went to Arab-led parties, a record. Most of the Jewish-led opposition parties have ruled out partnering with them. That leaves both sides short, and the Arab parties holding the balance.

panels.caption: A record 19 seats for Arab-led parties.

scenes.narration: Netanyahu says the right wing has a clear majority. Eisenkot says voters showed no confidence in the government. Both are now trying to build a coalition.

bubble.text: The right-wing bloc has a clear, decisive majority.

panels.caption: Eisenkot: voters showed no confidence in the government.

scenes.narration: Results are certified this week. Then President Isaac Herzog meets every party and chooses who gets the first chance to form a government. That person has twenty eight days, which can be extended by fourteen.
Until then, the current government stays on as a caretaker. Sources are in the description.
